transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 10:30 AM EDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jonah Reed (Veridian CTO), Sarah Kim (ML Eng), Marcus Li (Head of Infra)
Shared: pricing deck (link: https://redwood.app/decks/pricing.pdf), benchmark spreadsheet (drive link provided after call)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, i'll kick us off. is the time still good for the 40 minutes?
[00:10] Jonah: yeah that works, thanks alex. quick intros — i'm jonah cto at veridian, we run a quant research platform, sarah and marcus are with me.
[00:16] Sarah: hi all.
[00:18] Marcus: morning.
[00:20] Priya: hi, priya from redwood infra, i'll cover technical bits on batching and private options.

[02:05] Alex: high level, we want to understand your workload and cost constraints so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. can you share monthly volume and latency expectations?
[02:20] Jonah: sure. our target is about 10 to 15 million tokens/month initially, likely grow to 40m within 6-9 months if things go well. latency needs are 200-350ms p50 for short prompts, spikes allowed for longer generation. budget — we're trying to keep hosted costs under $8k/month for the pilot if possible, but that is flexible if dedicated gives big savings.

[04:00] Priya: ok that's helpful. on redwood hosted pricing we do per-token billing plus an optional reserved plan for high throughput. we also have levers like batching and prefix/KV caching which can materially reduce per-token effective cost especially if you have repeat patterns.
[04:20] Sarah: can you quantify — like we saw claims about 3x cost reduction with caching, is that realistic?

[04:35] Priya: yeah aproximations vary; if your workload has repeated prefixes (like many prompts starting with the same system instructions or static context) and you can reuse KV cache, you can get 2-4x per-token reduction for the generator stage because you're not recomputing attention for cached tokens. for batching, if you can tolerate a slight 20-50ms latency hit, you can get much higher throughput and lower GPU amortized cost, roughly 20-50% cost reduction depending on batchability. these numbers are workload dependent.

[06:10] Jonah: how does that compare with dedicated? like if we reserve a slot, what's the rough per-token?
[06:20] Alex: dedicated is more of a commitment model — you pay for reserved capacity and get lower unit price. as a rough example, for your scale (10-15M tokens/month) dedicated could be 30-60% cheaper per-token versus hosted depending on utilization. but that assumes you keep utilization high; with bursty traffic you might need burst/backfill pricing.

[07:05] Marcus: what's the math? i.e. if we use 15M tokens, what's hosted cost vs dedicated? can you send a model?
[07:12] Alex: yes we'll send a sample cost model; i'll attach a spreadsheet that shows scenarios — per-model per-token rates, expected batching gains, caching assumptions.

[07:50] Sarah: also curious about quantization/ model variants — does redwood have cheaper quantized runs or smaller models we can use for specific tasks?
[08:05] Priya: yes, we support quantized variants and smaller model families. in hosted we offer curated model catalog and optimized kernels. dedicated/private gives you more choice about pinned model variants and custom quant profiles. frequently we'll recommend a two-tier model routing — high-precision model for critical gen and a smaller / quantized model for high-volume cheap transforms.

[09:40] Jonah: security question — for a pilot we can't send PII out. what's the hosted policy on data retention and KMS?
[09:50] Alex: hosted supports customer opt-out of retention and we integrate with KMS for encryption at rest. we'll also share SOC2 docs. for stricter regimes private or VPC deployment is available where you control the network and keys.

[11:30] Marcus: regarding VPC/private — if we go private on prem or VPC, do we still get same batching/caching benefits or is there performance difference?
[11:45] Priya: you get the same runtime benefits — our runtime works across hosted/dedicated/private. perf differences typically come from infra (network, GPU type). for example on-prem with older GPUs may have different latency/cost tradeoffs. we can profile your infra in the deep dive.

[13:00] Jonah: back to numbers — alex, you said you'll send sheet. can you walk quickly through the sample spreadsheet now?
[13:10] Alex: sure, i'll summarize — column A is model choice, B is tokens/month, C is batchability factor (0-1), D is cache hit rate, E is effective tokens billed. final is cost. example: for 15M tokens, with batch factor 0.6 and cache hit 0.25, effective billed tokens drops to ~10m and hosted cost comes in around $10k/month on the conservative hosted per-token. with dedicated, same assumptions could be ~$5.5k/mo but you'd need commit and variance in month to month could change that. these are illustrative.

[15:05] Sarah: what do you assume for per-token pricing in the hosted conservative case?
[15:10] Alex: depends on model; for the medium open model we reference $0.0008 per prompt token and $0.0016 per completion token in the conservative example — again these are example tiers and i'll send exact published ratecard.

[16:30] Marcus: burst — our traffic is spiky end of day, can redwood handle burst without huge overage?
[16:40] Priya: yes, we have burst pools and automatic fallback routing to compatible model variants and regions. dedicated customers can configure burst capacity or auto-scale; hosted has quota policies but we can set soft-budgets and throttles. if you need guaranteed low-latency during spikes, dedicated with reserved burst is best.

[18:20] Jonah: what's the onboarding time for a pilot? two weeks? a month?
[18:30] Alex: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: week 1 gather sample prompts/creds, week 2 run benchmark and iterate, week 3 analysis and tuning. if you need private deployment it's longer due to infra provisioning.

[20:00] Sarah: for the benchmark what do you need from us?
[20:10] Priya: sample prompt set, expected QPS distribution (1min granularity if possible), token length distribution, choice of models to test, and temporary read-only access to data or synthetic samples. we prefer a small S3 bucket or drive link.

[21:30] Jonah: any gotchas on caching — e.g. when does cache miss happen or cause correctness issues?
[21:40] Priya: cache is safe for prefix/context reuse; correctness only changes if your prompts mutate system-level instructions that should not be reused. also long KV cache can increase memory usage; we size caches and have TTLs. we'll help pick safe cache policies in the POC.

[23:05] Marcus: network egress — if using hosted we'll have egress costs on our side, right?
[23:15] Alex: yes egress/ingress between your infra and hosted endpoints can incur cloud egress. for Dedicated we can collocate in your VPC to reduce that. private on-prem solves egress entirely.

[24:40] Sarah: about observability — can we get token-level cost breakdowns per-route? this matters for our product analytics team.
[24:50] Alex: yes Redwood Console gives token-level cost, latency by route/model, and per-token breakdown. we can turn on higher retention for a fee.

[26:00] Jonah: what's the procurement cycle? we are mid-market but need SOC2 + terms review.
[26:10] Alex: typical procurement for pilot is lightweight — we have standard SAs and data protection addendums. for enterprise private we go through legal, SOC2, and custom terms. i'll loop in our sales ops.

[27:30] Priya: small note on model selection — for your use case many customers use a smaller quantized model for reranking and cheap transforms, and a larger model for final generation. routing can be automatic so you only pay high unit cost when needed.

[29:00] Jonah: curious about the worst-case cost — if caching doesn't help and batching isn't possible, what's the hosted ceiling?
[29:12] Alex: ceiling depends on model; worst-case hosted raw per-token could be 2-3x the optimized number in our spreadsheet. i'll call out conservative and optimistic scenarios in the sheet.

[30:40] Sarah: do you have any public benchmarks for similar customers?
[30:50] Alex: we have anonymized benchmarks and case studies; i'll share a short one pager and a benchmark spreadsheet template.

[32:10] Marcus: if we want dedicated, are we locked to specific GPU types or can we change?
[32:20] Priya: you can configure GPU series; there are lead times for hardware changes. for dedicated pools you pick instance types and autoscale parameters.

[33:40] Jonah: pricing negotiation — what flexibility is there on committed volumes?
[33:50] Alex: we can do committed monthly/annual discounts for Dedicated and Reserved; hosted has volume tiers. for pilot we usually do hosted credits + a short trial.

[35:00] Sarah: can we do a quick scenario — say 15M tokens, no caching, low batchability, what's the hosted cost estimate?
[35:10] Alex: quick back-of-envelope — 15M tokens * $0.0008 = $12k if all tokens charged at prompt rate; realistic split prompt/completion and some batching lowers it to ~9-11k. i'll refine in spreadsheet.

[36:40] Marcus: ok that's helpful. do you have a short SLA for hosted trial?
[36:45] Alex: hosted has best-effort trial SLAs; Dedicated includes SLOs. for pilots we can set an ops point-of-contact.

[38:00] Jonah: next steps recap?
[38:05] Alex: i'll send pricing deck, sample cost model spreadsheet, SOC2 link, and benchmark template by friday (2026-03-06). priya will schedule the infra deep dive. veridian team to share sample prompts, token distribution, and qps by next tuesday (2026-03-05).

[39:10] Sarah: sounds good. one more thing — can you include example quantized model performance numbers?
[39:20] Priya: yes, i'll include typical latency and token-cost deltas for our quant profiles in the doc.

[40:05] Jonah: great, thanks all.
[40:10] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and action items.
[40:20] (call ends)
